No . Backyard failure. Southern , Shore. Have not seen a here for a couple of years. Until now, other small pollinators have been abundant. Not this year. Hardly any bugs at all. Picture shows a nice fence covered with scarlet runner beans...been blooming for about three weeks...and only about 4 beans set on the whole thing. Tomatoes also have hundreds of flowers and only a few fruit set. Very discouraging for the future.
A momma carpenter bee has discovered one of the starter holes I drilled a few weeks ago. She is kicking out sawdust like crazy but seen here taking a break.

I welcome any other suggestions because I am at a loss. It doesn't matter what I do in my yard to promote health for our shared earth if a goddamn HOA upstream can just poison the waterways and kill everything. I'm certain that my bees (which were doing great!) are done for and the fruit trees by the creek may be damaged/contaminated. I don't know a way to save them.

As I was going on another errand, I think I found the culprit for the fishkill and general insect death in the neighborhood (including my honey bees) for the last 3 years. A company hired by the HOA upstream of my location (less than a mile) has been dumping at least 4 goddamn chemicals into the ponds with a goddamn fire hose, which directly drain to the creek that flows by my house and into a near by tributary.

I've been furiously documenting everything - taking pictures, taking water samples, and calling IDEM, and the local stormwater utility. I know from my certification as a Hoosier River Watch volunteer that this shows all the signs of utterly ignorant behavior that is causing ecological harm! And not just to the plant life, invertebrates, and aquatic life, but to humans as well. I mean, kids fish in those ponds for God's sake!!

Sadly, the bees mostly left and didn't go into the nearby swarm boxes. So at least they aren't in the building, but those (very likely) diseased bees are still in the environment and going to hurt other colonies. The comb and honey I removed were tossed, and the several thousand bees I caught were euthanized, an unfortunate and necessary part of caring for the bees. Protecting the local population is more important, though it sucks.

Bee day! Two packages rehoused, settled, and fed. Trying one more time to see if my neighbors and community will stop killing my bees with pesticides. Found out from a sympathetic neighbor that the tiny creek (nee drainage ditch) that runs thru my backyard had dead fish in it last year further upstream. Cool cool cool. After I called, the city is now testing the water... I guess I'll know by June, one way or another.

Sorry that you're in the same boat! What happened in your case, if it can ask? For me, it was neighbors using pesticides and potentially a polluted creek that the bees use all the time. (I replaced queens 3x times last year!! Then every quarter or so, queen was verified dead. No wasps were even sighted all year, and a huge drop in fireflies...fish dead in the water.)

Thanks! Unfortunately here, I had a massive increase in mosquito spraying and at least one documented instance of a bunch of dead small fish in the creek they use. This may be the last year I try if my neighbors don't change their behavior. I hope you fare better this year!
